evidence_results.name: restricted_algebra

value.name: Latent covariance inversion
value.assumptions: Known conditional latent phenotype variance V(m), both zygosity covariances K_MZ(m),K_DZ(m), common family moderator, equal A/C/E across zygosity, genetic correlations1/.5; model correctly specified and variances positive.
value.derivation: V=A+C+E, K_MZ=A+C, K_DZ=A/2+C. Thus A=2(K_MZ-K_DZ), C=2K_DZ-K_MZ, E=V-K_MZ. Substitution gives the identity exactly.
value.verification: SymPy simplifies each substituted difference to0.
value.limit: This assumes latent covariance functions are identified/known; it does not prove their identifiability from finite binary item vectors.

value.name: Logvariance coefficients at two moderator levels
value.assumptions: Two distinct m0,m1; known positive variance values V0,V1 for a component; V(m)=exp(beta0+beta1*m).
value.proof: Take logs. The2x2 design matrix has determinant m1-m0≠0, hence beta1=(log(V1)-log(V0))/(m1-m0), beta0=log(V0)-beta1*m0 uniquely. Same argument covers continuous support containing two distinct levels, conditional on known variance function.
value.limit: One moderator value does not identify both coefficients. Injectivity does not ensure a finite or unique likelihood maximum.

value.name: Binary path sign indeterminacy
value.assumptions: Shared binary moderator0/1; component path a+b*m; variance is its square; no restriction requiring the path positive at both endpoints.
value.proof: Replace b by -2a-b while keeping a fixed. Endpoints are a and -(a+b), so both squared endpoint values are unchanged. Global(a,b)→(-a,-b) is an additional symmetry. With nonzero a and a+b there are four sign combinations before restrictions; a>0 removes only the global pair. Degenerate zero endpoints can merge solutions.
value.limit: Equality is for shared-moderator covariance endpoints, not arbitrary separate-twin moderator cross-products.

value.name: Continuous moderator qualification
value.assumptions: Two affine paths agree after squaring at at least three distinct real moderator values.
value.proof: Their squared difference is degree≤2 with at least three roots, so it is the zero polynomial. Its factorization is [(a-u)+(b-w)m][(a+u)+(b+w)m]. R[m] is an integral domain, so one affine factor is identically0: (u,w)=(a,b) or(-a,-b). If both intercepts are strictly positive, only equality remains.
value.verification: Symbolic polynomial factorization identity passes; exact midpoint witness distinguishes the binary-only reflection:9/25 vs1/100.
value.limit: Global sign ambiguity persists on continuous support unless a sign convention is imposed. This does not say the source global-sign statement is false, nor address all full-model likelihood modes.

value.name: Monotonicity of loglinear variance
value.proof: d exp(beta0+beta1*m)/dm=beta1*exp(beta0+beta1*m), with strictly positive exponential. Thus increasing when beta1>0,decreasing when beta1<0,constant when beta1=0.
value.limit: Monotonicity of a variance curve is unrelated to convexity/concavity of the marginal likelihood.

evidence_results.scope: Covariance inversion, logvariance two-level recovery, binary sign symmetry, continuous support qualification and variance monotonicity.

evidence_results.name: finite_sample_MLE_qualification

value.target: Unqualified assertion that the logvariance parametrization gives one finite maximum for every data set, p72; not an allegation about the empirical fits.
value.data: Any finite nonempty collection of twins with every observed Rasch item response0; include both MZ/DZ and both binary moderator levels if desired. Known finite item difficulties; finite model parameters with positive variances.
value.proof: Write each latent trait theta_ij=mu+Z_ij, with joint distribution of Z fixed when other parameters are fixed. Conditional probability of all observed zeros is Q(mu,Z)=product_ijk logistic(b_k-mu-Z_ij). Every factor lies strictly between0and1 and strictly increases as mu decreases, so E[Q] is strictly increasing as mu decreases for every finite parameter vector. By dominated convergence E[Q]→1 as mu→−infinity. At any finite mu,E[Q]<1. Hence the likelihood has supremum1 but no finite maximum; adjusting mu improves every finite candidate even in the full model. This disproves the unqualified existence-and-uniqueness implication, not population identifiability.
value.Bayesian_limit: A proper normal prior on mu changes the posterior objective; this likelihood counterexample neither proves posterior impropriety nor multimodality. Source Bayesian fits and population identification are separate questions.

evidence_results.scope: All-zero response likelihood has supremum1 but no finite maximum; separate from population identification and proper Bayesian posterior.

evidence_results.name: conditional_joint_item_identification
value: Two distinct binary observations, conditionally independent given the same scalar theta; repeating the same binary outcome is not a second observation.
Known finite slopes a1>=a2>0 and finite d1,d2; relabel the higher-slope item to provide the held-fixed marginal p. The population joint probability q is for these same two item observations.
theta=mu+sZ with standardnormal Z, finite mu and s>0; relevant population p andq are identifiable from the observation design.

For the ACE bridge: finite strictlypositive conditional ACE variances, shared familymoderator, known MZ/DZ correlations1and1/2, common conditional latent mean/variance acrosszygosity, fixed anchored calibration and conditional measurement independence.

For each of two distinct moderatorlevels, both MZ andDZ groups and the needed within-person/cross-twin moments have positive observed support or separately justified identification. Positive marginal group/moderator support alone is insufficient.
